name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+29 partisan lean in a St. Louis-area district
Incumbent Wesley Bell running with $1.1M on hand and outside support
Republican challenger Paul Berry has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 98%
model.rationale: The district's D+29 lean, Bell's incumbency and strong fundraising, and a Republican challenger with no visible resources all point to a safe Democratic hold; markets agree at roughly 98%. No polls or expert ratings exist, but nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Bell underperforming the district's lean, or unexpected outside spending against him, would be the first sign of trouble.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Wesley Bell, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks reelection in a St. Louis-area district with a D+29 partisan lean, one of the most Democratic seats in Missouri. He enters the general election with about $1.1 million on hand after raising $3.6 million, plus outside support on his side. Republican Paul Berry reports no fundraising, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets price a Bell win near 98%. The seat is rated Safe Democratic.
